citation.authors: Dolezsar CM, McGrath JJ, Herzig AJM et al

record.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of perceived racial discrimination and blood pressure
record.finding: Perceived racial discrimination was associated with hypertension (small effect, Z 0.048, 95% CI 0.013 to 0.087) but not with resting blood pressure. The link was stronger among men, Black participants and older people, and strongest for night-time ambulatory blood pressure in Black participants.
record.note: Small associations; the authors note methodological limitations. Abstract read.
